source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Ask whether the client understands and accept a yes-or-no response as confirmation","B":"Provide written instructions only and avoid asking the client to explain them","C":"Use teach-back and ask the client to explain key instructions in their own words","D":"Assume understanding from education level rather than checking comprehension"}}
source_row.rationale: The "teach-back" method — asking the client to explain instructions or demonstrate a skill in their own words — is a recommended, evidence-based technique to confirm true understanding, since simply asking "Do you understand?" often yields an inaccurate yes/no response that does not reliably indicate comprehension, particularly important for clients with limited health literacy.
source_row.source_detail: Teach-back checks understanding by asking the patient/caregiver to explain information in their own words; 3rd edition toolkit, accessed 2026-08-14.
